content.title: About
content.content: Mashed potato from fast food is a ready‑to‑eat side dish made from boiled potatoes that are mashed to a smooth consistency and typically enriched with butter, milk, and salt. It is served hot alongside burgers, chicken nuggets, and other fast‑food items.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fast‑food mashed potatoes are usually made from high‑starch potato varieties to achieve a fluffy texture.
In the United States, more than 30 % of all restaurant potato sales are mashed potatoes.
To speed up service, many chains use pre‑blended mixes stored in chilled units and prepared in 2–3 minutes.
Mashed potatoes can be offered in classic buttery flavor or with cheese, garlic, or herb variations.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Mashed potatoes retain some vitamin C, an antioxidant important for immune health.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Starch provides readily available carbohydrates that fuel the body quickly.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When made from whole‑potato varieties, a modest amount of fiber remains, aiding digestion.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The smooth texture makes it suitable for children and people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Fast‑food versions are often heavily salted, which can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Added butter and milk increase calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy should choose dairy‑free versions.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Some pre‑made mixes may contain partially hydrogenated oils; checking the ingredient list is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the mash hot as a side to meat, chicken, or fish dishes. It can be topped with cheese, fresh herbs, garlic sauce, or seasonings of choice. For a healthier option, select versions without added butter or excess salt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared mash in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to at least 60 °C before serving.
